title: Who gets more chikki: two sharing one, or eight sharing five?
description: One chikki is divided between two children, and five chikkis among eight children. One half is written as four eighths, so both shares are counted in the same unit and compared. Keeko doubts the answer by looking only at how many children share.
teaching_notes: One idea: to compare two shares, first write them in the same fractional unit, then compare the number of units. Watch for students who decide by the number of children alone.

source: In which group will each child get more chikki: 1 chikki div
video_script.why: A learner compares one half with five eighths by writing one half in eighths, so both shares are counted in the same unit.
video_script.substitution: the book's own groups: one chikki between two children and five chikkis among eight children
video_script.anchor: one chikki divided between two children, and five chikkis divided among eight children
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko decides by the number of children alone and says the pair gets more, although the second group also has five chikkis instead of one.
video_script.payoff_line: each child in the second group gets more chikki

final_answer.spoken: one half is four eighths, which is less than five eighths, so each child in the second group gets more

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, four eighths, five eighths

names.Jia: the child who writes one half as four eighths
names.Leeza: the child who says we must compare one half and five eighths

never_show: a tick on the first group
maths_rules: group 1: 1 chikki divided between 2 children, each child gets 1/2 chikki
group 2: 5 chikkis divided among 8 children, each child gets 5/8 chikki
4/8 < 5/8 because both are counted in eighths and 4 eighths is fewer than 5 eighths
so each child in group 2 gets more
slip: Keeko says group 1 gets more because only 2 children share there, and ignores that group 2 shares 5 chikkis, not 1
video_script.design: Two groups stay on the board all video. One half is rewritten as four eighths so both shares sit in the same unit. Keeko's doubt counts children alone.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; group 1: two children with one chikki; group 2: eight children with five chikkis of the same size; the words which group gets more? appear

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.g1: two children and one chikki appear on the left
marks.g2: eight children and five chikkis of the same size appear on the right
marks.ask: the words which group gets more? appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it is about sharing chikki.
<bookmark mark='g1'/>In one group, one chikki is divided between two children.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>In the other group, five chikkis are divided among eight children.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>In which group will each child get more chikki?

beats.on_screen: the two groups hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the first chikki splits into 2 halves labelled 1/2; the five chikkis each split into 8 pieces and one child collects one piece from each, labelled 5/8; 1/2 and 5/8 sit side by side

marks.half: the first chikki splits into 2 halves labelled 1/2
marks.eighths: the five chikkis each split into 8 equal pieces and one child collects one piece from each, labelled 5/8
marks.pair: 1/2 and 5/8 sit side by side with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>In the first group, each child gets one half of a chikki.
<bookmark mark='eighths'/>In the second group, each child gets one eighth from every chikki, which makes five eighths.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>One half counts halves, and five eighths counts eighths, so the two fractional units are different.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 chikki between 2 children; 5 chikkis among 8 children
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one chikki is divided between two children, and five chikkis are divided among eight children.

beats.on_screen: To find: the group where each child gets more
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the group where each child gets more chikki.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: each child's share as a fraction: group 1 gets 1/2, group 2 gets 5/8; compare 1/2 and 5/8

marks.shares: the two shares 1/2 and 5/8 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='shares'/>Step one, write each child's share as a fraction. One chikki between two children gives one half.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>Five chikkis among eight children gives five eighths. Leeza says we must compare one half and five eighths.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 1/2 = (1 x 4)/(2 x 4) = 4/8; multiply top and bottom by the same number

marks.rule: the rule multiply top and bottom by the same number is written
marks.four: 1/2 changes to (1 x 4)/(2 x 4) and then to 4/8

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, write one half in eighths. Jia multiplies the top and the bottom by the same number, which keeps the amount the same.
<bookmark mark='four'/>One times four over two times four is four eighths.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: both shares in eighths; compare the numbers of eighths: 4 and 5

marks.units: 4 eighth pieces and 5 eighth pieces are lined up one above the other

narration: <bookmark mark='units'/>Step three, both shares are now counted in eighths, so we compare the number of eighths. One share has four, and the other has five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 4/8 < 5/8, so each child in group 2 gets more

marks.ans: 4/8 < 5/8 is written and glows, and group 2 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Four eighths is less than five eighths, so each child in the second group gets more chikki.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two groups
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says group 1 gets more because only 2 children share; the five chikkis of group 2 light up; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears over group 1
marks.five: the five chikkis of group 2 light up
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and 1/2 = 4/8 appears again

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the first group gets more, because only two children share there.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Fewer children is true, but the second group also has five chikkis, not one chikki.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Counting children alone cannot decide this. We write both shares in the same unit and compare.
